label: B2B CRM — "We already have one"
objection: We've been on Salesforce for years, and the team finally knows how to use it. Switching to another CRM sounds like a lot of disruption for something I'm not sure we even need.

exchanges.rep: I get that. Replacing a system your team already knows would be a big ask. Atlas doesn't have to replace Salesforce right away — most teams start by running the two together and syncing the data while they evaluate it.
exchanges.reply: Okay, that's better than I was picturing. But if we're still using Salesforce, what would Atlas actually give my reps that they don't already have?

exchanges.rep: One of the biggest differences is automatic activity capture. Calls, emails, and meetings are logged without reps having to enter everything themselves, so your pipeline stays much more complete and up to date.
exchanges.reply: That would definitely help. My bigger concern is whether anyone would actually use it. We rolled out another tool last year, and half the team basically ignored it.

exchanges.rep: That's a fair concern. Atlas works through the inbox and calendar your reps are already using, so they don't have to remember to open another system every day. A lot of the activity gets captured without them doing anything extra.
exchanges.reply: That makes sense. Before I took it any further, though, I'd want to see what adoption actually looks like for a sales team about our size.

exchanges.rep: Absolutely. I can send you a couple of case studies from similar-sized teams, and we can also set up a two-week pilot using your own data so you can see how people actually use it.
exchanges.reply: That feels reasonable. I'll share the case studies with the team and see how everyone feels about trying the pilot.

feedback.performance: You handled the customer's existing-CRM objection well by showing that Atlas didn't have to mean an immediate replacement. That lowered the perceived risk and opened the door to discussing what the product could add. The conversation would be stronger if you established the business value more clearly before moving into adoption concerns.
feedback.key_strengths: You recognized that switching systems was the customer's first concern and addressed it directly. You also picked up on the deeper issue — whether the sales team would actually use the product — and responded with a specific explanation rather than a generic promise. Offering a pilot was a good way to reduce the risk of moving forward.
feedback.areas_to_improve: Give the customer a measurable reason to care about Atlas earlier in the conversation. For example, time saved on manual data entry or an improvement in pipeline completeness would make the value easier to weigh against the cost and effort of adding another tool.
